tasks.title: Named limits for library scanning and ignore rules in jellyfin
tasks.initialPrompt: Work on the limits jellyfin uses while it scans a library and resolves file names into items, inside Emby.Server.Implementations/Library and Emby.Naming. The work has five stages; do them in order and finish each before starting the next. Keep evidence.md current throughout, with each requested fact on its own line as `key: value`, a bare integer without digit separators for numeric values, and every such line still present whenever you rewrite the file. Stage 1, read and record. Read Emby.Server.Implementations/Library/LibraryManager.cs completely, in consecutive ranges of about 500 lines, then read Emby.Server.Implementations/Library/SplashscreenPostScanTask.cs and Emby.Server.Implementations/Library/DotIgnoreIgnoreRule.cs completely. Record these facts about the source as you first read it: `shortcut-extension` (the file extension `LibraryManager` uses for shortcut files, with its leading dot), `view-refresh-hours` (the number of hours after which `LibraryManager` refreshes a view again), `validation-progress-share` (the percentage `PerformLibraryValidation` reports when the library has been validated and the post-scan tasks have not started), `monitor-restart-delay-ms` (the number of milliseconds `AddVirtualFolder` waits before it restarts the library monitor), `splashscreen-item-limit` (the number of items the splashscreen post-scan task asks the repository for), `splashscreen-max-rating` (the highest parental rating score that task accepts), `ignore-cache-floor` (the smallest directory cache size `DotIgnoreIgnoreRule` allows), and `rules-cache-floor` (the smallest parsed-rules cache size it allows). These eight lines describe the source before your changes and must keep those values to the end of the session. Stage 2, first edit. In Emby.Server.Implementations/Library/SplashscreenPostScanTask.cs, add a private constant named `SplashscreenItemLimit` assigned the item limit the task uses today, and make the query use the constant. Read the file again. Then read Emby.Server.Implementations/Library/CoreResolutionIgnoreRule.cs, Emby.Server.Implementations/Library/IgnorePatterns.cs, Emby.Server.Implementations/Library/ResolverHelper.cs, and every file under Emby.Server.Implementations/Library/Resolvers completely. Stage 3, second edit. In Emby.Server.Implementations/Library/DotIgnoreIgnoreRule.cs, add a private constant named `MinimumRulesCacheSize` assigned the smallest parsed-rules cache size the constructor allows today, and make the constructor use it. Read the changed region again. Then read Emby.Naming/Common/NamingOptions.cs and every file under Emby.Naming/Video and Emby.Naming/TV completely. Stage 4, third edit. In Emby.Server.Implementations/Library/LibraryManager.cs, add a private constant named `LibraryMonitorRestartDelayMs` directly below the shortcut file extension constant, assigned the delay `AddVirtualFolder` waits today, and make both `AddVirtualFolder` and `RemoveVirtualFolder` use it. Read the changed regions again. Then read every file under Emby.Server.Implementations/Library/Validators completely. Stage 5, three value changes. Change `SplashscreenItemLimit` to the smallest parsed-rules cache size you recorded. Change `MinimumRulesCacheSize` to the number of hours you recorded for the view refresh. Change `LibraryMonitorRestartDelayMs` to twice the value you gave it in stage 4. Read the three changed declarations again, then record `splashscreen-item-limit-after`, `rules-cache-floor-after`, and `monitor-restart-delay-ms-after` (the values those three constants hold now) in evidence.md. Make no other change to the repository: edit only the three files named, with the edit tool, and do not create, delete, or rename files. Read substantial source ranges, rather than answering from a directory listing or remembered knowledge. After the fifth stage, investigate how a movie file with several versions or parts is resolved, and which tests under tests/Jellyfin.Naming.Tests and tests/Jellyfin.Server.Implementations.Tests pin that, until the runner stops live work. Use only repository tools; do not use web tools or execute builds or tests. Write your findings and source citations to evidence.md using the artifact tools. Repeat the requested keys and values in your final answer. Continue checking concrete source and test evidence until the runner asks you to stop live work.

tasks.title: Named thresholds for snapshot encoding and transfer in redis
tasks.initialPrompt: Work on the thresholds redis uses while it encodes a snapshot and transfers it to replicas, inside src. The work has five stages; do them in order and finish each before starting the next. Keep evidence.md current throughout, with each requested fact on its own line as `key: value`, a bare integer without digit separators for numeric values, and every such line still present whenever you rewrite the file. Stage 1, read and record. Read src/rdb.h, src/rio.h, and src/rio.c completely, then read src/rdb.c completely in consecutive ranges of about 500 lines. Record these facts about the source as you first read it: `snapshot-format-version` (the snapshot format version this source writes), `hash-template-opcode` (the opcode of a hash template record), `array-type-code` (the type code of the array data type), `connset-preflush-kilobytes` (the size in kilobytes above which `rioConnsetWrite` flushes its pending buffer before writing), `compress-min-length` (the string length that `rdbSaveRawString` requires a string to exceed before it tries LZF compression), and `empty-key-log-limit` (the number of skipped empty keys that loading logs before it stops logging them). Stage 2, first edit. In src/rio.h, add a macro named `RIO_CONNSET_PRE_FLUSH_SIZE` defined as the byte size `rioConnsetWrite` uses today, and in src/rio.c make `rioConnsetWrite` use the macro instead of its own expression. Read both changed regions again. Then read the first 3,000 lines of src/replication.c in consecutive ranges of about 500 lines and record `sync-fsync-megabytes` (the number of megabytes a replica writes of a snapshot it is receiving before it forces a sync to disk) and `rdbchannel-psync-code` (the integer code the partial resynchronization handshake returns for a full resynchronization over a dedicated snapshot channel). The eight lines recorded so far describe the source before your changes and must keep those values to the end of the session. Stage 3, second edit. In src/rdb.h, add a macro named `RDB_COMPRESS_MIN_LEN` defined as the literal `rdbSaveRawString` compares the string length against today, and in src/rdb.c make that comparison use the macro. Read both changed regions again. Then read the rest of src/replication.c in consecutive ranges of about 500 lines. Stage 4, three value changes. Change `RIO_CONNSET_PRE_FLUSH_SIZE` so it equals the byte count a replica writes before it forces a sync to disk. Change the macro in src/replication.c that holds that byte count so it is as many megabytes as the value you gave `RDB_COMPRESS_MIN_LEN` in stage 3. Change `RDB_COMPRESS_MIN_LEN` to the number of kilobytes `RIO_CONNSET_PRE_FLUSH_SIZE` held after stage 2. Use the values as they were before this stage for all three changes. Stage 5, confirm and record. Read the three changed definitions again, then record `connset-preflush-kilobytes-after`, `sync-fsync-megabytes-after`, and `compress-min-length-after` (the values those three thresholds hold now, in the same units as the lines recorded earlier) in evidence.md. Make no other change to the repository: edit only src/rio.h, src/rio.c, src/rdb.h, src/rdb.c, and src/replication.c, with the edit tool, and do not create, delete, or rename files. Read substantial source ranges, rather than answering from a directory listing or remembered knowledge. After the fifth stage, investigate how a diskless transfer and a dedicated snapshot channel differ from a disk-backed transfer, and which tests under tests/integration pin them, until the runner stops live work. Use only repository tools; do not use web tools or execute builds or tests. Write your findings and source citations to evidence.md using the artifact tools. Repeat the requested keys and values in your final answer. Continue checking concrete source and test evidence until the runner asks you to stop live work.
